enonce_intro_markdown: Given that $\tan\theta = \sqrt{3}$ and $\theta$ is an acute angle.

questions.corrige_markdown:
$\tan\theta = \dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{1}$. Draw a right-angled triangle with opposite side $\sqrt{3}$ and adjacent side $1$.

Hypotenuse: $\sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{4} = 2$.

$\sin\theta = \dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

**Answer: $\sin\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.**
